summary.one_liner: An open-source SDK (TypeScript and Python) for AI agent safety that blocks prompt injections, redacts PII and secrets, and scans repositories for agent-targeted attacks.
summary.what_it_does: The SDK exposes a guard method that classifies input and flags prompt injections, malicious instructions, and unsafe tool calls at runtime, returning a block or allow classification with violation types. A redact method removes PII, PHI, and secrets from text using a chosen model such as openai/gpt-4o-mini. A scan method analyzes repositories for attacks aimed at AI agents, such as repo poisoning, and returns a security report with usage cost. A test method for running red team scenarios against a production agent is marked as coming soon. The README also lists a CLI and an MCP server for use with Claude Code and Claude Desktop, alongside the SDKs.
use_cases: block prompt injections in agent input
redact PII and secrets from text
red team an AI agent before release
filter unsafe tool calls at runtime
add safety checks to a Python or TypeScript AI app
notable: Guard, redact, and scan methods available in both TypeScript and Python SDKs
Redaction covers PII, PHI, and secrets
Open-weight models can run Guard on your own infrastructure with 50-100ms latency per the README
MCP server for use with Claude Code and Claude Desktop
caveats: The test (red team) feature is marked as coming soon
An API key from superagent.sh is required (SUPERAGENT_API_KEY)
Running Guard on your own infrastructure requires open-weight model deployment; the README gives no setup details for this
keywords: remove emails and ssn from text
scan github repo for ai attacks
